sections.title: سعادت حسن منٹو (تعارف)

paras.text: Saadat Hasan Manto was born in the village of Sambrala (Ludhiana). His father's name was Khwaja Ghulam Hasan. Manto's early education took place at home. Manto's academic record was not very good, and the surprising thing is that he often failed in Urdu. Manto was interested in literature from his student days. He began his literary life with translations of foreign stories, but soon began to write creative stories. Besides this he went on earning money by writing stories for radio and films. After the creation of Pakistan he moved from Bombay to Lahore. Manto's last years passed in great poverty.

سعادت حسن منټو

زېږېدنه: ۱۹۱۲ز · مړینه: ۱۹۵۵ز

منټو د اردو ادب یو مهم او شخړه‌لرونکی لنډې کیسې لیکونکی دی. نقادان یې پرمختګ‌پال بولي خو پرمختګ‌پال یې له منلو انکار کوي. هغه د انسان له ژوند او ارواپوهنې سره بشپړ اشنا دی. هغه زیږ حقیقت په بې‌رحمۍ سره موضوع کړ او لوستونکي یې حیران کړل. هغه د حساس طبیعت او دقیقې کتنې هنرمند و. د منټو تصنیفات او تخلیقات بېلابېلو ژبو ته ژباړل شوي.

تصنیفات: اتش پارې، د منټو افسانې، لوګی، لذت سنګ، چغد، سړه غوښه، یزید، د نمرود خدايي، د پاچاهۍ پای او نور.

paras.text: When he was admitted to the hospital his condition was very bad. The first night he was put on oxygen. Nurse Jones was on duty; she thought this new patient would die before morning. His pulse was uncertain — sometimes it fluttered violently and sometimes it beat after long pauses.

sections.theory:
Manzoor — Saadat Hasan Manto

When he was admitted to the hospital his condition was very bad. The first night he was put on oxygen. Nurse Jones was on duty; she thought this new patient would die before morning. His pulse was uncertain — sometimes it fluttered violently and sometimes it beat after long pauses.

His body was drenched in sweat; he found no rest even for a moment. Sometimes he turned on this side, sometimes on that. When his restlessness grew too great he would sit up and begin taking long, deep breaths. His colour was yellow like a lump of turmeric. His eyes were sunken. The bridge of his nose was like a lump of ice. His whole body trembled.

Manzoor — Saadat Hasan Manto

When he was admitted to the hospital his condition was very bad. The first night he was put on oxygen. Nurse Jones was on duty; she thought this new patient would die before morning. His pulse was uncertain — sometimes it fluttered violently and sometimes it beat after long pauses.

The bridge of his nose was like a lump of ice. His whole body trembled.
